findings.claim: Findings 7 and 8 (and designs A7/A8) are sourced from stale copies in `.claude/worktrees/agent-*/`, not from the repo's canonical files, so the diagnosis may not match the tree the plan will edit.
findings.evidence: `cited_paths` resolves `migrate-job.yaml`, `serviceaccount.yaml`, `images.yml` and `tests.yml` ONLY under `.claude/worktrees/agent-*/` copies (e.g. 'EXISTS migrate-job.yaml -> 4 matches (.claude/worktrees/agent-a4fbeab64d564f480/infra/k8s/base/migrate-job.yaml, ...)'), while the file tree contains no `.github/` at all and does contain `infra/github`, which the analysis never mentions. Finding 8 itself admits reading multiple checkouts ('Both checkouts I found already set persist-credentials: false'). The analysis cites `infra/k8s/base/deployment.yaml` (which does exist at top level) alongside `migrate-job.yaml` as if both were the live manifests.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-verify findings 7, 8 and 9 against the actual working tree (`infra/k8s/base/*`, `infra/github/*`), state the canonical path of every cited manifest/workflow, and re-derive A7/A8 from those files before the plan edits them.

findings.claim: Design A1's core claim — that a PVC preserves hosted configuration 'with no code change' — contradicts finding 1's own description of `seed_home` and is never verified.
findings.evidence: Finding 1: '`sellbird/home.py` `seed_home` copies the shipped defaults into it on each start' and training 'writes `sellbird.local.yaml` ... there' so it does 'not survive a restart'. A1: 'a volume keeps all of them with no code change'. If `seed_home` overwrites existing files on each start (which finding 1's wording allows), the PVC alone still loses `sellbird.local.yaml` and `skills/product_knowledge.md` every restart; the analysis never checks whether `seed_home` is non-destructive for existing files.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify `seed_home`'s overwrite semantics and, if it clobbers, either fix `seed_home` to skip existing files (and say so in A1) or change A1's rationale.

findings.claim: In-scope items from the assess handoff — SEC-04, the JWKS https rule, and F1–F3 — have no finding and no design call, yet the analysis declares 'READY to spec. Nothing is blocked.'
findings.evidence: assess.handoff.json: 'Also in scope: migration Job ServiceAccount deadlock, JWKS https rule, DNS policy, F1-F3 and the Trivy control' and 'SEC-03, SEC-04, SEC-05'. Analysis.md labels findings for SEC-03 and SEC-05 only; 'SEC-04' never appears; JWKS https and F1–F3 appear only as a passing line in library-candidates.json `build_required` ('JWKS https rule, DNS policy for NodeLocal DNSCache, F1-F3 ... Small fixes in Sellbird's own code and manifests') with no gap analysis or design decision anywhere in analysis.md.
findings.suggested_fix: Add findings and design calls (or an explicit deferral with rationale) for SEC-04, the JWKS https rule and F1–F3 before declaring readiness.

findings.claim: The Trivy control is only partially designed: A8 covers gating deploys on tests, but the rest of the required control (image ID recorded before scans, Trivy checksum, failing-scan enforcement) has no design call.
findings.evidence: library-candidates.json `build_required` names the full need: 'Deploy gated on green tests; image ID recorded before scans; Trivy checksum and failing-scan control', and the goals mention 'fix first-run failures, including the Trivy control'; A8's call is only 'Merge the test jobs into the path to `deploy`' and the Readiness table maps A8/A9 to 'supply chain' generically without covering the scan control.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend A8 (or add a design call) covering image-ID capture before scans, the Trivy checksum/verification step and the failing-scan gate, since the plan must fix the Trivy first-run failure.

findings.claim: The hash-locking gap evaluates exactly one candidate and one rejected alternative, omitting the main competing solutions and the repo's own existing lock.
findings.evidence: The only candidate is `uv`; the only rejection in analysis.md A9 is 'Hand-maintained hashes'. Never considered: `pip-compile --generate-hashes` (pip-tools), `poetry export --with-hashes`/`pdm export`, or building the image on `uv sync` with the already-present top-level `uv.lock` (the file tree lists `./uv.lock`, while the candidate calls it 'an untracked uv.lock' and proposes a second, differently-formatted `uv pip compile` output that would then have to be kept in sync with it).
findings.suggested_fix: Record a verdict against pip-tools and against driving the build from the existing uv.lock (or state why the dual-lock approach is preferred), and name where the compiled requirements file lives so it cannot drift from `uv.lock`/`requirements.txt`.

findings.claim: A3 and A4 are both conditioned on 'hosted mode' but the analysis never defines how hosted mode is detected, leaving the smallest runtime changes untestable as written.
findings.evidence: A3: 'In hosted mode, `_needs_setup` stops requiring a `.env` file'; A4: 'In hosted mode, report running from the heartbeat's last recorded cycle'; no config flag, env var or manifest marker for 'hosted mode' appears anywhere in the findings or design table, and A2's sidecar container depends on the same notion.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the hosted-mode signal (e.g. an explicit `SELLBIRD_HOSTED=1` env set only in the Deployment) so plan-level acceptance criteria can be written unambiguously.
